revision_note: v2 of this draft responds to the 2026-09-02 external design review (request-changes): PR #96 boundary integrated, design renamed and identification limits stated, power recomputed by the committed noncentral-t planning script, verdict decision table written out in full, interim formulas specified and type-I error validated by committed Monte Carlo, completion-conditioned estimand made explicit with a hard >4-replacement termination rule, dose model replaced by a within-seed linear contrast, and the budget reduced to three named packages. No experiment may start against this document; it carries no SHA freeze.

preconditions: Z8 cross-cohort H~Q structure analysis complete (per-cohort fits only); if the discovery-side correlation sign is bootstrap-unstable, all moderation narrative is struck from this protocol before freezing
Z2-upgraded noise floor complete: 3 checkpoints x 5 generation seeds + 1-2 same-seed retraining segments; sigma_e recorded in primary_endpoint.planning_assumptions
planning_calculations.py rerun with any revised sigma/sd assumptions; planning_calculations.json re-committed
type_I_error_simulation.py rerun under the frozen parameters; unconditional empirical type-I error under both null scenarios <= 0.055
protocol_lint.py passes on the final protocol.json
freeze_procedure.freeze_action: sha256sum of the four named files -- protocol.json, interim_futility.py, planning_calculations.py, and planning_calculations.json -- written to protocol.sha256; the freeze commit timestamp must precede the first line of any stage-1 training log
freeze_procedure.note: This file is a DRAFT. No experiment may start against it. Amendments before freeze are unrestricted; after freeze, only outcome-blind amendments with authorization records (same standard as q256_fresh_crossed_switch_n12_matpool_v1).

design.name: matched two-history continuation under a fixed current-A policy (two arms per seed: AA and BA)
design.naming_rationale: The earlier label 'two-arm crossed-history continuation' is retired: with only AA and BA this design is NOT crossed. It identifies exactly one contrast, H_A, under one fixed continuation policy.
identification_limits: estimable: H_A = the effect of prior spacing history (g=1.1 vs g=1.0, 0-512 kimg) on future quality under a fixed current-A continuation (512-1024 kimg)
NOT estimable: the current-policy main effect (no current-B arm)
NOT estimable: the history x current-policy interaction
NOT estimable: whether the history effect transports across continuation policies; PR #95 and PR #97 remain the crossed evidence for H_B and I_switch; this cohort only independently confirms H_A
design.temporal_regime_boundary: PR #96 (B@384 pulse-chase, 10 seeds, sealed 60/60 evaluation) found INFORMATIVE_NULL: a shorter B exposure from 384 to 512 kimg leaves no detectable quality carryover after a shared A continuation to 640 kimg, within the frozen 3% margin. The route-3 cohort therefore tests a different temporal regime: a longer 0-512 kimg spacing history followed to 1024 kimg. Read together the two experiments bound the mechanism: not every short-lived spacing difference leaves a detectable future-quality effect; the carryover question this cohort addresses is specific to the full 0-512 kimg history scale.
design.rationale_data: fresh n=11: corr(C1,C2)=0.965 between the two continuation contrasts, so the second continuation is nearly redundant for the history effect. Exact noncentral-t planning (planning_calculations.py, committed): at equal budget (~96 RE) two-arm n=24 has power 0.947 at the fresh H_A point estimate (0.938 at the pooled-H point estimate; both recorded) versus 0.783 for four-arm n=16, and assurance 0.823 versus 0.697. Computed from published H_C_I_Q_G_per_seed.csv (SHA256 4d8bc83f7e9254878294a38fc3ad2ac40c84445d497dd166cec4f37b2e197461); design-planning use of unblinded data; no new inference.

arms_per_seed.stage1: A history (g=1.0) and B history (g=1.1), 0 -> 512 kimg, full state saved at 512
arms_per_seed.stage1b: both histories continue under current-A, 512 -> 1024 kimg (AA and BA; AA passes through the same switch-resume machinery as BA, no-op verified by parity gate)

design.training_commit_semantics: identical to protocol q256_fresh_crossed_switch_n12_matpool_v1 (batch=128, batch_gpu=16, q=256, canonical CIFAR-10 SHA256 08c9ed1b2b1c523268dc0f05a0569dd654209aea46197e3f56ec149dd714f372)
design.evaluator: frozen evaluator commit d6aba02fb88e9db0993623895eb2228ed717d810, FP32, FID50k NFE1 primary; blind sealed evaluation matrix identical in mechanism to the n=11 protocol

primary_endpoint.estimand_population: completion-conditioned: the mean of H_A over seeds in the completer population (seeds, including replacements, for which both arms finish and are evaluated). This is explicitly NOT the unconditional effect over the started-seed population; if B-history training terminates more often, the primary estimand conditions on that instability. The B-arm termination rate is therefore preregistered as a coprimary-reported secondary endpoint so the conditioning is always visible next to the estimate.
primary_endpoint.test: one-sided paired t-test on mean(H_A), H1: E[H_A] < 0, alpha = 0.05

planning_assumptions.sd_source: fresh n=11 SD(H_A); to be replaced by the noise-floor-informed value if Z2-upgrade shows a material evaluation-noise share
planning_assumptions.power_at_fresh_point_estimate: 0.947 (exact noncentral-t; 0.938 at the pooled-H point estimate; planning_calculations.py)
planning_assumptions.assurance_at_fresh_posterior: 0.823 (flat prior on the effect; posterior N(-0.0776, 0.1129/sqrt(11)) from the fresh cohort; predictive power by order-200 Gauss-Hermite quadrature of the exact noncentral-t power; planning_calculations.py; assumes cohort exchangeability)
planning_assumptions.honesty_clause: This design has 80% power only for effects >= 0.059; the fresh point estimate is -0.078 and its 95% CI includes zero. A null or inconclusive outcome is a live possibility and its reporting is prespecified below.

inputs: p1 = one-sided paired t p-value for H1 mean(H_A) < 0
lo95, hi95 = two-sided 95% t CI on mean(H_A)
lo90, hi90 = two-sided 90% t CI on mean(H_A) (TOST bounds)
neg = count of seeds with H_A_s < 0 out of the analyzed n

categories_in_precedence_order.name: STRONG_SUCCESS
categories_in_precedence_order.condition: p1 < 0.05 AND hi95 < -DELTA AND neg >= 22 of 24
categories_in_precedence_order.note: 22/24 is the proportional adaptation of the n=11 rule (>=10/11, i.e. >=91%); the exact cut is pinned at freeze before any data exist

categories_in_precedence_order.name: INFORMATIVE_PRACTICAL_NULL
categories_in_precedence_order.condition: lo90 > -DELTA AND hi90 < DELTA (TOST rejects at 10%)
categories_in_precedence_order.note: takes precedence over WEAK exactly as in the frozen n=11 rules, so a precise but tiny negative effect is read as practical equivalence, not replication

categories_in_precedence_order.name: WEAK_DIRECTIONAL_REPLICATION
categories_in_precedence_order.condition: NOT strong AND NOT equivalent AND hi95 < 0
categories_in_precedence_order.note: hi95 < 0 implies two-sided p < 0.05 and hence p1 < 0.025; p1 < 0.05 ALONE is deliberately insufficient. Edge case fixed by this table: if p1 < 0.05 but hi95 >= 0, the verdict is INCONCLUSIVE (this is exactly the fresh n=11 configuration).

verdict_decision_table.gatekeeping_link: Gatekeeping step 1 (below) is passed iff the verdict is STRONG_SUCCESS or WEAK_DIRECTIONAL_REPLICATION. A one-sided rejection with an INCONCLUSIVE verdict does not open the chain.
verdict_decision_table.provenance: identical category mechanics to the frozen n=11 statistics.py (verified against analysis/q256_fresh_crossed_switch_n12_matpool_v1/statistics.py on the PR #97 branch): strong > equivalent > weak > opposite > inconclusive precedence, TOST band log(1.03), sign-count criterion scaled proportionally

gatekeeping_chain.rule: fixed-sequence; each step tested at full alpha only if the previous step passes; step 1 passes iff the verdict is STRONG_SUCCESS or WEAK_DIRECTIONAL_REPLICATION
gatekeeping_chain.step1: verdict per verdict_decision_table (one-sided alpha 0.05 on H_A)

step2.name: dose trend, within-seed linear contrast
step2.design: nested arm on preselected seeds [51..58]: g=1.2 history (0->512) + current-A continuation (512->1024); the g=1.0 and g=1.1 endpoints are the AA and BA arms of the SAME seeds from THIS cohort (no reuse of unblinded n=11 results)
step2.contrast: per-seed within-seed linear contrast on terminal log-FID@1024/NFE1: L_s = -0.5*Y_{s,g=1.0} + 0*Y_{s,g=1.1} + 0.5*Y_{s,g=1.2} (equally spaced g-1.0 in {0, 0.1, 0.2}); no random effect, no cross-seed regression
step2.test: two-sided paired t-test on mean(L) over the 8 seeds, alpha = 0.05 (two-sided because the discovery/fresh corr(H,Q) signs conflict; no directional prior is defensible); co-reported exact two-sided sign-flip permutation p-value on the mean (full 2^8 = 256 enumeration, test named in full per reporting_rules)
step2.power: 0.899 at the linear projection E[L] = fresh mean(H_A); MDE(80%) = 0.078; SD planning value sd(H_A)/sqrt(2) = 0.0798 (Var(L) = 0.25*Var(Y_1.0)+0.25*Var(Y_1.2), equal independent per-arm endpoint noise), to be replaced by the Z2-upgraded noise floor at freeze (planning_calculations.py)
step2.missing_data: a terminated g=1.2 arm is replaced from the ordered replacement pool under the same rule as the primary (replacement decided before any 1024 evaluation of that seed is decoded); if the pool is exhausted, the dose analysis falls back to complete-contrast seeds with a tipping-point sensitivity, and this fallback is reported
step2.claim_level: spacing-schedule dose at the policy level; channel attribution (target vs weight) is explicitly out of scope and deferred to the archived stage-2 regime experiment

step3_optional_module.name: horizon extension
step3_optional_module.design: extend AA/BA of the preregistered first 12 seeds by seed number (or all 24 if the full package is frozen) from 1024 to 2048 kimg; endpoint H_A@2048
step3_optional_module.test: one-sided alpha = 0.05, only if steps 1 and 2 both pass
step3_optional_module.activation: which horizon tier (none / 12-seed subset / full cohort) is fixed at freeze time by the budget package; if excluded, it may be preregistered later as a same-cohort extension BEFORE any 2048 evaluation exists
step3_optional_module.framing_rule: decay of the effect at 2048 is reported as persistence-timescale characterization, not as refutation; prewritten reading: decay supports the mid-training-misranking thesis (rankings drift on this timescale)

interim_analysis.type: binding futility-only; zero alpha spend (no efficacy stopping)
interim_analysis.timing: after seeds [51..62] (first 12 by preassigned seed number, NOT by completion order) complete both arms and their 1024 evaluations under seal
interim_analysis.mechanism: committed script interim_futility.py (SHA256 recorded in protocol.sha256) emits a single token {CONTINUE, STOP-FUTILITY}; sealed numerical log written to evidence/interim_sealed/, decoded only at final database lock; no effect estimate, sign, or magnitude disclosed to any author before final lock
interim_analysis.sign_free_sd_definition: s12 = sample standard deviation (ddof=1) of the 12 observed H_A values. SD is invariant to the sign of the effect, and no author sees any value: the committed script consumes sealed values and emits only the token. The same s12 is the sigma used in the conditional-power formula.
interim_analysis.conditional_power_formula: CP = Phi( (-t_{0.95, n_f-1} * s12 * sqrt(n_f) - S12 - (n_f - 12) * delta_design) / (s12 * sqrt(n_f - 12)) ), with S12 = sum of the 12 interim H_A values, delta_design = -0.0776 (fresh H_A point estimate; re-frozen if Z2 revises the planning assumptions), and n_f the final sample size selected in the same step (24, or 28 if the SD trigger fires). This treats s12 as known sigma; the committed script implements exactly this expression.
interim_analysis.stop_rule: STOP-FUTILITY iff mean(H_A,12) > 0 OR CP < 0.20. Under the null, P(mean(H_A,12) > 0) = 0.5 by construction, so half of null cohorts stop at interim; this is intended futility behavior, not a defect.

blinded_sd_reestimation.action: final sample size extends to the preset cap n_f = 28 using additional seeds [83, 84, 85, 86] in preassigned order
blinded_sd_reestimation.alpha_impact: the final one-sided t-test runs at df = n_f - 1 with no alpha adjustment; the blinded SD trigger is a function of the data that is invariant to the sign of the effect, and under normality the sample mean and SD are independent, so the sample-size choice cannot condition the test away from the null

monte_carlo_validation.results: unconditional empirical type-I error 0.0495 under the planning SD (extension fired 5.3%) and 0.0490 under the stress SD = 0.20 (extension fired 86.0%); both <= 0.055 acceptance bound. The diagnostic rate given continuation (~0.099) is inflated by selection on the interim mean sign and is NOT the procedure type-I error.
monte_carlo_validation.refreeze_rule: any change to interim_n, cap_n, sd_trigger, cp_threshold, or the stop rule after freeze requires rerunning this simulation and re-verifying the acceptance bound before the change is authorized

missing_data.termination_criterion: identical to n=11 protocol: second non-finite loss event in any arm, validator-enforced
missing_data.primary_population: replaced cohort n=24: a terminated seed is replaced by the next seed in the ordered replacement pool, decided before any 1024-kimg evaluation of that seed is decoded; at most 4 replacements
missing_data.hard_termination_rule: if MORE than 4 replacements would be required, cohort execution STOPS: no primary verdict is rendered, the cohort is reported as EXECUTION_FAILED with the termination ledger, and any further use requires a new outcome-blind authorization record. The five verdict categories are never adjudicated on a cohort with >4 replacements
missing_data.estimand_note: the replacement rule makes the primary estimand completion-conditioned (see primary_endpoint.estimand_population); the paper must state this estimand next to the estimate
missing_data.secondary_instability_endpoint: count of B-history-arm terminations, reported with arm identity (instability is itself carryover-relevant evidence)
sensitivity_analyses: all-started-seeds tipping-point: every terminated seed, replaced or not, imputed at H_A = +/- 2*SD, report whether the primary conclusion flips (this is the analysis that does NOT condition on completion)
complete-case on started seeds (no replacement), reported for contrast with the n=11 protocol's original primary
B-arm vs A-arm termination rates with exact two-sided binomial p-value, reported as instability evidence, not as a quality-effect claim

transplant.design: at the 512 switch: 2x2 {A-history, B-history} x {RAdam-moments reset, no reset} on 3 preselected seeds (2 largest-|H| candidates from planning data + 1 randomly drawn, rationale recorded), continuation-A to 1024; plus EMA-swap and params-swap variants each with a sham arm (self-transplant through the same machinery) that must pass verify_parity.py no-op standard or the module is void
transplant.go_no_go: EMA-swap arm runs only if analytic EMA residual weight w = 2^(-512/t_half) >= 0.05 (G0-c)
transplant.status: exploratory; no hypothesis test; cannot appear in the abstract as evidence; manipulation check = first-8-kimg loss shift vs pre-switch 32-kimg mean, reported not inferred

exploratory_modules.scorecard: before any exploratory module runs, each named hypothesis (EMA inertia / moments channel / dose monotonicity / persistence) records its predicted sign per module in evidence/scorecard.json; post-hoc reporting is restricted to hit/miss against this table

descriptive_analyses.persistence_regression: H_A_s = alpha + rho * Q_s + eps with errors-in-variables correction rho_c = S_HQ / (S_QQ - 2*sigma_e^2) using sigma_e from the Z2-upgraded noise floor; alpha_c = mean(H_A) - rho_c * mean(Q); BCa bootstrap CIs; estimation only, no test
descriptive_analyses.moderation_clause: No inferential claim about H-Q moderation will be made at any n achievable in this project. All Q-segment displays use sample quantiles, not preregistered thresholds.
descriptive_analyses.cross_cohort_synthesis: descriptive random-effects synthesis of the two preregistered cohorts (n=11, n=24) may be displayed, labeled 'descriptive synthesis, not a hypothesis test'; the no-merged-single-test rule stands
descriptive_analyses.pr96_junction: PR #96's INFORMATIVE_NULL is presented adjacently as the short-exposure boundary of the mechanism (see design.temporal_regime_boundary); no pooled analysis across the two protocols is performed because the exposure and horizon definitions differ

reporting_rules.verdict_categories: the five categories defined in verdict_decision_table, applied to H_A with the equivalence band +/- log(1.03); the table is normative, not 'same as previous protocol'
wording: sign counts always accompanied by magnitudes
reversal statements always carry eligibility definition (Q threshold), frequency, and magnitude
the words 'magnitude bracket' are banned; n<6 exploratory outputs report per-seed point values only, with the preregistered sentence 'no interval or directional statement is made'
any sign-flip/permutation p-value is named in full ('exact permutation test on the mean under sign flips') with a code pointer and the 'not a decision input' qualifier where applicable
the primary estimate is always accompanied by the completion-conditioned estimand sentence and the B-arm termination count

budget_packages.note: three named packages; every document (runbook, protocol, PR body) must reference these names and numbers only. Mixing numbers across packages is the inconsistency this v2 revision eliminates.

MINIMAL.a100_hours_all_in: ~400 (5% rerun margin per measured failure rate included)

WITH_HORIZON_SUBSET.training_re: 149 = 127 + 22 (1024->2048 extension, first 12 seeds by seed number, both arms)

budget_packages.comparison: fresh n=11 actual all-in was ~253 A100·h; the minimal package is the committed floor and fits the post-G5 calendar; the horizon tier is chosen at freeze

target_venues: ICML 2027 (late-January deadline) or TMLR; ICLR 2028 explicitly rejected as calendar opportunity cost
